Reasoning prose first, then JSON.

REASONING

The request — "project how recharge will change by 2050 under a warming climate scenario" — has a mechanistic goal (how does recharge respond to warming) and an implicit prediction goal (a 2050 value). The controlling execution reality dominates the design: the framework's forcing is **historical only, NLDAS-2 1980–2018**. There is no future/GCM-downscaled forcing and no climate-scenario capability. Therefore the question **as posed (a 2050 projection under a warming scenario) is not answerable** by this stack — you cannot force ELM with a 2050 climate you do not have. Presenting a "2050 projection" would be fabrication.

What the stack CAN honestly deliver is (a) a present-day, spatially-resolved recharge baseline for the Naches, and (b) an empirical **climate sensitivity of recharge** using two feasible proxies within 1980–2018: a warm-dry vs cool-wet year contrast (temporal delta) and an elevation gradient acting as a space-for-time thermal/precip analog (NLDAS is elevation-resolved across this 1625 m-relief basin, so precip/temperature genuinely vary with the columns). This yields a defensible dQrecharge/dT and dQrecharge/dP that a hydrologist could then apply to any external 2050 delta — but the delta itself must come from outside the stack.

Recharge is a slow subsurface flux (QDRAI/QRECHARGE): the design MUST include a WTD-informed warm start (Fan 2013) plus spin-up years, or the numbers are cold-start artifacts. There are **no observations** listed for this domain, so recharge validation is a genuine gap — I flag it rather than invent SNOTEL/well data.

Driver "climate" is expressed here through elevation via NLDAS forcing. I stratify by elevation band (which sets snow fraction, rain-snow transition, precip) crossed with SSURGO soil (which sets how that water partitions into recharge vs runoff). I concentrate columns at the rain-snow transition, where warming most strongly shifts snow→rain and thus recharge timing/magnitude.
